newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks weak in morning after Greenspan comments.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks weak in morning after Greenspan comments.

text.p: Interest rate jitters pushed Hong Kong stocks lower in morning trade on Thursday after U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan hinted on Wednesday that the central bank may need to raise rates in coming months.
But analysts said expectations of solid earnings growth in Hong Kong and keen interest in China-related issues was providing support.
The Hang Seng Index was down 32.26 points, or 0.24 percent, at 13,509.57 after falling to an early low of 13,425.83.
Turnover was HK$2.45 billion after the first 45 minutes of trade.
"The market is not collapsing," said Howard Gorges, a director at South China Brokerage.
"I think there has been an expectation for some time that Greenspan is itching to find an excuse to put rates up and it is likely to happen sooner rather than later."
Greenspan told the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday that the Fed may raise rates before inflation picks up.
"It is conceivable...to have to move before you see actual evidences of real inflation emerging," Greenspan said.

Some analysts said that U.S. economic data were not strong enough to warrant a rate increase just yet, but Ricky Tam, research manager at Delta Asia Securities, expected economic data for March to show stronger growth.
"The Fed might wait until May (to raise rates)," Tam said.

Gorges said a quarter-point or half-point rise in U.S. interest rates should not hurt the Hong Kong market "unless people think they are going up and up". If Wall Street stocks suffered a selloff, Hong Kong would find support from interest in China-related shares and earnings momentum, he added.

"Wall Street has been breaking record highs for nearly two years. It (a selloff) will have some effect on Hong Kong but Hong Kong also has the China factor becoming more important and so the effect may not be as strong as it has sometimes been in the past," Gorges said.
February Hang Seng Index futures, which expire on Thursday, were down 75 points at 13,480.
Shares in HSBC fell HK$1.50 to HK$192.00.
Among the China-related issues, Shanghai Industrial rose HK$0.70 to HK$33.70 and China Overseas added HK$0.05 to HK$4.725.
